variants.headline: Shipbuilding for the colony route
variants.sub: Shipbuilding by the home world has provided a larger vessel or another vessel for the colony route.
variants.body:
The home world has built a larger ship or an additional ship for the colony route. The construction is a transport development, not an announcement of arrival. In assessing {target}, readers should distinguish provision of a vessel from an unreported schedule, cargo or immediate change in supplies.

Transport is part of the material relationship between the colony and the home world. Our principles require attention to how that relationship serves people, not simply admiration for a vessel. The political question is what responsible provision means, and it cannot be settled by inventing a promised benefit.

We welcome {target} in this assessment. Construction for the route deserves recognition as a tangible development, even while a fair account keeps that achievement distinct from promises about voyages not established here. Political principle should remain visible when judgment becomes less comfortable.
